3063: Numbers that are prime or one less than a prime.
3064: Practical numbers: positive integers m such that every k <= sigma(m) is a sum of distinct divisors of m. Also called panarithmic numbers.
3065: Interpolate 0's between each pair of digits of n.
3066: Positive integers k that are not divisible by A002034(k).
3067: Primes in the progression (n! + m)/m where n advances by 1 and m resets to 1 upon each prime occurrence.
3068: a(n) = least prime of the form n*k! + 1.
3069: Smallest k such that there are as many composite numbers less than n as there are between n and k.
3070: a(1)=1, a(2)=2; thereafter successive products of pairs of digits make further digits.
3071: Even integers k such that there exists a prime p with p=min{q: q prime and (k-q) prime} and k < p^3.
